title: espOS firmware project
description: One firmware project that can be installed on an espOS device. Mirrors the RegistryProject type in signalk-espos-manager; CI validates every entry against this file.

id.description: Short identifier; must equal the filename without .json.

app.description: The firmware's CMake project() name — what the device reports via mDNS and /api/v1/system/ping, and what espOS matches an update manifest against. NOT the repository name, and NOT espos_start_opts_t.app_name. Getting this wrong means devices never find their updates, with no hint why.

summary.description: One line describing what the firmware does.

repo.description: GitHub owner/repo. Releases are read from here.

boards.description: Boards this firmware supports. Declare every one: espOS matches an update on chip alone, so when two incompatible boards share a target the flasher has to ask which the user has — the wrong image is usually a black screen.

flashMinBytes.description: Smallest flash this firmware fits. A 16 MB partition table on a 4 MB module fails or half-works.

reportedAs.description: The board string this board's firmware reports verbatim in GET /api/v1/system/info -> hardware.board (espOS opts.board). Matched EXACTLY, never fuzzily: it is what decides whether an over-the-air update may be offered, and a near-miss would install firmware for a different display. Omit it when the firmware does not report a board; the update is then withheld rather than guessed.

assetSegment.description: The segment this board's release assets carry, as captured by the `board` named group in assets.ota/assets.merged (e.g. "7b" in p4_cockpit-v1.3.0-7b-ota.bin). Compared case-insensitively. Without it a board-labelled asset cannot be tied to a board, and the build is not offered over the air.

assets.description: Anchored regexes matching the release assets. A `version` named group is required; a `board` named group is needed when a release carries one image per board, and its value is matched against each board's assetSegment. Without a board group a release with several assets is not indexed at all, rather than one being picked arbitrarily.

signingKeyId.description: Stable identity of the signing key these releases use — the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the public key, not the key itself. A device only accepts firmware signed with the key it was flashed with, so changing this strands every device already in the field.

signed.description: False when releases are built with a throwaway key: those flash over USB but accept no updates afterwards.

official.description: Maintained by the signalk-espOS organisation. Set by maintainers only.

deprecated.description: True, or a sentence saying what to use instead.

webAssetsBranch.description: Branch of `repo` carrying the release images, laid out as <tag>/<asset>. GitHub serves release downloads without an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so a browser cannot fetch them; raw.githubusercontent does send one. Declare this and the index also publishes mergedWebUrl/otaWebUrl pointing there, which is what the web flasher uses. Without it a project's firmware can only be installed from the Signal K plugin, which fetches server-side and is unaffected.

esposSubmodule.description: Path of the espOS submodule inside `repo`, when it is not the default "espos". The reindexer reads the pin at each release tag and records the espOS version that release was built against, so a consumer can say whether a build predates a runtime fix. An exact tag match only: a project pinned to an untagged commit records no version rather than a wrong one.
